brief: Recognize speculation in a volatile asset without treating past gains as evidence of safety.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Past Performance"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Ganancias pasadas no protegen"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Ganhos passados não protegem"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Recognize speculation in a volatile asset without treating past gains as evidence of safety.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A recent price jump tells you what happened, not what your money is guaranteed to do next.
instruction.misconception: Recent gains, popularity or excitement demonstrate safety of a speculative asset.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the visible fictional amounts and conditions; earlier arithmetic is preparation, not a hidden financial assumption.

evidence.reasoning: A token rose yesterday. Buying solely because someone else may pay more tomorrow is speculation, not evidence of safety.
A past price change does not guarantee the next one.
The purchase relies on an uncertain future buyer’s price.
Attention does not establish a limit on future losses.
A small purchase can still lose its invested amount.
Selected winners do not describe everyone’s risk.
Future buyers and prices can differ from last year’s.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.
